status: Independent (ChatGPT) verification of PRs #23-#25 found 4 blocking findings before merge. All 4 fixed on the same open PRs, with new adversarial tests. Not merged yet -- awaiting re-verification.

worker_runtime_suite.note: was 44; +18 from the fix-verification round (12 approval-gate tests, 1 real-timeout-kill test, 2 bounded-result tests, 5 worker-health-separation tests, minus overlap)

core_v2_prototypes_regression.note: unaffected by this round's fixes; unchanged from the prior 161

independent_verification_findings_and_fi.finding: Approval gated job completion, not execution -- a worker's sandboxed handler ran unconditionally at lease time; approval state was only checked afterward at complete()
independent_verification_findings_and_fi.fix: added WorkerJobQueue.execute() as the sole path to invoking a capability's action; for any authority_requirement != NONE, action() is only ever called from inside the reused ApprovalEngine.execute() (never duplicated), which validates approval state, executor identity, expiry, and an exact arguments digest, then atomically consumes the approval into EXECUTED. complete() now requires EXECUTED (was APPROVED) as defense in depth. Wired through transport.execute() into worker_client.py.

independent_verification_findings_and_fi.finding: Timeout enforcement was a post-return elapsed-time check, not a real deadline -- a hung/CPU-bound handler was never actually interrupted
independent_verification_findings_and_fi.fix: handler now runs in a forked child process under a hard deadline; on overrun the child is terminated (SIGTERM then SIGKILL) and the call fails closed
tests_added: test_scenario_14_timeout_is_a_real_kill_not_a_post_hoc_check (proves an actual kill via a marker file the handler would only write after its full sleep -- the marker never appears)
independent_verification_findings_and_fi.bug_found_while_fixing: a real multiprocessing deadlock: waiting via process.join(timeout) before draining the result pipe hangs whenever a handler's result exceeds the pipe's kernel buffer (~64KB) -- the child blocks mid-write, the parent isn't reading, and every oversized-result test spuriously 'timed out'. Fixed by waiting on the connection (parent_conn.poll(timeout)) as the primary deadline gate, which starts draining as soon as data arrives.

independent_verification_findings_and_fi.finding: Only stdout_summary was bounded; the structured output result and evidence_files were not
independent_verification_findings_and_fi.fix: added MAX_RESULT_BYTES (64KB, refuses rather than truncates a structured dict) and MAX_EVIDENCE_FILES (20)

independent_verification_findings_and_fi.finding: A worker heartbeat could set arbitrary coordinator-owned scheduling state (heartbeat(..., status=ANY_WORKERSTATUS)), letting a worker force itself AVAILABLE while actually BUSY on a live lease (or the reverse), bypassing mark_busy()/mark_available()
independent_verification_findings_and_fi.fix: heartbeat() now accepts only an optional WorkerHealth (HEALTHY/DEGRADED), never a raw WorkerStatus; BUSY is untouchable by a worker's own heartbeat in either direction; DEGRADED is honored only out of non-BUSY states

defects_found_and_fixed_prior_to_indepen.defect: WAITING_FOR_APPROVAL -> FAILED was not a valid transition, so a denied approval on any approval-gated job would raise an unhandled JobStateError instead of failing the job
defects_found_and_fixed_prior_to_indepen.found_by: exercising job_protocol.WorkerJobQueue.deny() with a synthetic approval-required capability (scenario 17's test setup)
defects_found_and_fixed_prior_to_indepen.fix: added JobState.FAILED to the WAITING_FOR_APPROVAL transition set, plus a new parametrized test case in job_model/tests/test_jobs.py

defects_found_and_fixed_prior_to_indepen.defect: leaked the underlying job_model.JobStateError instead of wrapping it as JobProtocolError, breaking the module's own exception-boundary contract

called workers.mark_available() unconditionally; crashed with WorkerRegistryError if the worker's status wasn't exactly BUSY/DEGRADED (e.g. a job leased via WorkerJobQueue.lease() directly rather than through poll_for_job's mark_busy path) -- inconsistent with finalize_failure(), which already guarded this
defects_found_and_fixed_prior_to_indepen.fix: wrapped mark_available() in the same defensive try/except finalize_failure() already used

defects_found_and_fixed_prior_to_indepen.defect: no module in the actual runtime path ever imported capabilities.py, so sandbox._HANDLERS would be empty (no capability could ever execute) unless something happened to import it first
defects_found_and_fixed_prior_to_indepen.found_by: first test run against real capability handlers (11 failures, all "no registered handler")
defects_found_and_fixed_prior_to_indepen.fix: worker_client.py now imports capabilities.py for its registration side effect, since it's the module that actually calls run_capability
